sourceEvidence.label: E1 feasibility study exact source snapshot and four supplied review findings

assessment.summary: The repeated loader-spelling bypass supports one structural hardening opportunity: retain exact-byte projection and replace negative spelling recognition with a fail-closed declared-source capability grammar. Three independent truth and CLI defects still require direct fixes under every option.

nonNegotiables: Read each bounded projected source once and hash and parse those exact bytes.
Fail closed before Phase 0 on an unknown dependency-sensitive source capability.
Preserve ordinary safe object operations and the two exact PEP 562 package initializers.
Do not claim a Python sandbox or complete runtime dependency proof.
Retain direct fixes for decision/report propagation, exact snapshot paths, and verify exit status under every option.
Do not run implementation validation or any study phase while planning or implementing this hardening.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
The target remains a local deterministic demo rather than a production inspection system.
The written specification is approved and the implementation plan has passed independent review; the user must explicitly authorize one execution mode before any production edit.
No repository code, tests, validation, or study commands were executed for this analysis.

opportunities.title: Make declared source dependencies a positive capability boundary
opportunities.summary: Preserve the exact-byte projection and express accepted source capabilities positively instead of enumerating new reflective loader spellings after review finds them.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current visitor owns a growing set of syntax-specific recognizers. That structure can reject known loader spellings but cannot make the open-ended Python reflection surface closed; adjacent artifact and CLI findings also show why verification credit and process success must propagate through explicit dependencies rather than complements or generic success paths.

evidence.claim: The supplied review identifies vars(builtins)["__import__"] as the latest accepted reflected-loader spelling; exact-revision source recognizes selected names, attributes, getattr calls and __dict__ subscripts but not this call-wrapped namespace access.
The projection reader hashes each bounded payload and retains the same payload for ast.parse, then builds declared edges, direct allowlists and forbidden reachability from that snapshot.
A positive capability grammar is a more stable control owner than another deny predicate because unknown dependency-sensitive reflection can fail closed without first naming its spelling.
Malformed decision JSON can return an invalid state that marks decision.json invalid without propagating invalidity to a present dependent report.md.
Snapshot validation checks names and bytes, accepts any original path with a broad user-directory prefix, and does not compare either path to the two exact frozen tuples.
The CLI prints every non-exception verify result and then returns zero without inspecting result.status.study_valid.
The root package and E1 package initializers are the two intended PEP 562 lazy-export sites and both use literal maps plus import_module inside module-level __getattr__.

desiredInvariants: Every declared production source file is read once within the existing bounds, and the bytes hashed into the projection are the bytes parsed for policy.
Every accepted project dependency is a declared, projected and allowed source edge before Phase 0.
Unknown loader, executable-code or dependency-sensitive reflection capability syntax fails closed in runtime-reachable projected source.
Only the exact root and E1 package initializer paths may use the structurally exact PEP 562 lazy-loader form.
Ordinary safe object operations remain available through finite positive forms rather than a broad reflection exemption.
A report receives verification credit only through a verified decision dependency; snapshot identity includes both exact paths and bytes; verify exits nonzero for study_valid=false.
The resulting claim is declared source dependency closure, not sandboxing or complete semantic runtime reachability.

options.title: Continue incremental spelling patches
options.summary: Add vars(builtins) and adjacent negative fixtures while directly repairing the three independent truth and CLI defects.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A new predicate can reject the known vars(builtins) spelling, but adjacent unmodeled spellings remain recurrence risk.
Central invalidity propagation must be added directly; loader predicates do not affect report credit.
Both canonical snapshot paths must be compared directly before reading bytes.
The verify command needs an explicit domain-invalid exit mapping.

tradeoffs.assessment: The four known cases can be closed, but the import control still depends on reviewers finding every relevant spelling.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add exact regressions for all four findings and challenge the visitor with adjacent loader acquisition forms.

tradeoffs.assessment: A few AST predicates and path comparisons add no runtime hop and little work to the existing scan.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare dependency-scan wall time on the same 47-path projection; any repeatable regression requires review.

tradeoffs.assessment: The option adds bounded fixture and predicate state without a new long-lived structure.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS for the same projection and investigate any repeatable increase.

tradeoffs.assessment: Explicit report propagation and exit semantics improve failure signaling, while denylist omissions remain possible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise malformed decisions, path aliases and invalid domain reports and assert deterministic fail-closed results.

tradeoffs.assessment: Shell automation would see invalid verification, with no new service or deployment component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Capture JSON output and process status for valid PENDING, valid terminal and invalid reports.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing scanner and public APIs remain, so rollout and rollback are focused; future patch churn is the long-term cost.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run focused compatibility coverage for the current projection and both lazy initializers before broader validation.

residualRisks: A new reflective loader spelling can bypass the visitor.
Tests may create false confidence by enumerating examples rather than the capability invariant.
The direct fixes remain independently safety-critical.

workPackages: Add the known reflection predicate and regression matrix.
Propagate decision invalidity to report credit.
Freeze both snapshot paths and map invalid verify results to nonzero.
acceptanceCriteria: All four supplied findings fail closed without changing the frozen study inputs.
Both PEP 562 initializer compatibility cases remain accepted.
migrationNotes: Preserve current direct protections throughout rollout.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Before study execution, revert the focused change. After evidence is generated, invalidate it and restart the freeze gate.

options.title: Adopt a static positive source-capability grammar
options.summary: Keep single-read hashing and AST parsing, but accept only declared dependency edges and finite safe capability forms, with exact exceptions for two PEP 562 initializers.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The known bypass becomes a mandatory regression while unknown dependency-sensitive capabilities reject by default.
The selected option still directly centralizes decision-to-report invalidity propagation.
The selected option still freezes and compares both snapshot paths and the existing byte hashes.
The selected option still maps study_valid=false to a nonzero verify process status after printing JSON.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unknown loader, executable-code and dependency-sensitive reflection capabilities fail closed in the declared projection; semantic runtime behavior outside that source claim remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use positive and negative capability matrices, exact-byte swap cases and the original four regressions; separately review the bounded claim language.

tradeoffs.assessment: Lexical provenance and branch joins add work to the existing bounded AST walk but add no application runtime hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require the focused projected-source suites and make validate to complete within their existing fixed timeouts; confirm one parse and one bounded policy traversal per captured module, and add no standalone benchmark without a separate design update.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-scope provenance maps and branch unions increase transient scan memory while ASTs are live; no persistent cache or process is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review transient scope and branch-join bounds, require existing focused/full validation to complete without resource failure, and add no numeric memory gate without a separate design update.

tradeoffs.assessment: Stable capability categories and explicit truth dependencies improve deterministic failure, though conservative false positives can block legitimate future source.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run accepted ordinary-object fixtures, both initializer contracts and ambiguous binding cases; every rejection must identify module, line and capability family.

tradeoffs.assessment: There is no new deployment unit, and category diagnostics plus nonzero verify status improve automation; policy ownership becomes a review responsibility.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review diagnostic stability and CI/Make status propagation, and document the exception-review workflow.

tradeoffs.assessment: The visitor becomes a real lexical capability analysis and may require narrow refactors of legitimate reflection; exact initializer and public API behavior must remain compatible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory current reflection uses, prove finite safe forms, retain tactical guards, and gate broad validation behind written-spec approval.

residualRisks: Static AST policy does not prove all Python semantics, callback targets, descriptors, native extensions, environment effects or subprocess code.
A policy implementation bug can misclassify capability provenance.
The two initializer exceptions become trusted syntax and require exact structural regression coverage.

workPackages: Replace spelling provenance with lexical capability frames and fail-closed branch joins.
Validate literal declared edges and two exact PEP 562 initializer structures.
Retain finite ordinary-object operations and reject broad dependency-sensitive reflection.
Apply the three direct truth and CLI repairs before freezing the projection.
acceptanceCriteria: Known and adjacent capability-family cases fail closed while current safe object operations and both initializers pass.
Hashing and parsing use one captured byte payload per source path.
Reader-facing claims say declared source dependency closure and explicitly deny a sandbox claim.
All four supplied findings have focused regression evidence after implementation.
migrationNotes: The written specification is approved and the implementation plan has passed independent review; production edits remain blocked until the user explicitly authorizes one execution mode.
Future dynamic Python requires a narrow reviewed exception or non-reflective refactor.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Before any study execution, revert the grammar and direct fixes. Once validation or study artifacts exist, invalidate them and restart from an absent result root and newly frozen projection.

options.title: Enforce imports through a runtime bootstrap
options.summary: Install an import guard before loading the study runner, retain static inventory checks, and directly repair the three independent truth and CLI defects.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The guard can block exercised forbidden imports after installation, but it does not prove unexercised or pre-bootstrap behavior.
Decision/report invalidity still needs a direct artifact-state repair.
Snapshot paths still need direct exact tuple comparison.
CLI domain-invalid status still needs direct process-status mapping.

tradeoffs.assessment: A guard observes actual post-bootstrap imports, but preloaded modules, pre-bootstrap code, unexercised branches, subprocesses and native loading remain outside the claim.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise allowed and forbidden imports before and after installation and enumerate every path that bypasses the hook.

tradeoffs.assessment: The entry point adds hook decisions to import startup; steady-state impact should be small after module caching but is unmeasured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure process startup, first-import latency and total verify duration against HEAD; require an approved budget before rollout.

tradeoffs.assessment: Guard state and import ledgers remain live for the process, though no service or persistent cache is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare startup and peak RSS with the same command and projection; investigate retained module or ledger growth.

tradeoffs.assessment: Hook ordering, module caching and bootstrap failures add new initialization modes and can make behavior entry-point dependent.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test direct module invocation, CLI invocation, repeated imports, partial bootstrap failure and subprocess behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators need hook diagnostics and must distinguish static attestation from exercised runtime evidence.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define import-denial telemetry, startup failure messages and incident instructions before adoption.

tradeoffs.assessment: The current top-level runner import must move behind the guard, and every supported entry point needs compatibility coverage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory entry points and import order, stage a wrapper with the existing scanner retained, and prove rollback before any evidence is generated.

residualRisks: Already loaded modules and pre-bootstrap execution remain outside enforcement.
Subprocesses and native extension loading require separate controls.
The bootstrap is not a sandbox.

affectedComponents: artifact, protocol and CLI direct-fix components
workPackages: Move runner loading behind a fixed bootstrap.
Install and observe an import guard for the allowed runtime set.
Retain static projection inventory and the three direct truth/CLI repairs.
acceptanceCriteria: All supported entry points install the guard before runner import.
Forbidden exercised imports fail with stable diagnostics.
Documentation distinguishes runtime observations from declared source attestation.
migrationNotes: Treat this as a later defense-in-depth option unless runtime import evidence becomes a requirement.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore the original entry point before study execution. If guarded evidence has been produced, invalidate it and restart the freeze gate.

opportunities.recommendation: Select the static positive capability grammar under the current local, pre-execution and no-new-service constraints. Use incremental patches only for an emergency short horizon, and prefer runtime bootstrap only if exercised runtime-import enforcement becomes more important than pre-execution attestation and operational simplicity.

openQuestions: Should a future separately reviewed design add numeric scan-time or peak-memory budgets after the existing validation-runtime gate?
Which current ordinary reflection sites need finite positive forms versus small non-reflective refactors?
Should runtime bootstrap return later as defense in depth after the static design is implemented and validated?
